question: Which Mughal emperor ruled between 1713 and 1719?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Farrukh Siyar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Farrukh Siyar** was the Mughal emperor who ruled from **1713 to 1719**. His reign marked a politically unstable period for the declining Mughal Empire.
 
• Farrukh Siyar ascended the throne with the help of the influential Sayyid Brothers—**Abdullah Khan** and **Husain Ali Khan**, who acted as kingmakers during this period.
 
• He is known for granting several **farman** (imperial orders) to the British East India Company, which included **trading concessions** that laid the groundwork for British economic dominance in India.
 
• Farrukh Siyar's reign is marked by internal court intrigues, including his strained relationship with the Sayyid Brothers, who eventually deposed and executed him in **1719**.
 
• His reign witnessed a steep decline in the power and prestige of the Mughal Empire, with regional governors gaining autonomy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sayyid Brothers:**

 
 
• The Sayyid Brothers, known as the **"Kingmakers"**, were instrumental in Farrukh Siyar's rise to power. They held significant influence over the Mughal court during his reign.
 
• They deposed Farrukh Siyar when he attempted to reduce their influence, showcasing the weakening authority of the Mughal emperor.
 
 
 
• **British East India Company:**
 
 
• During Farrukh Siyar's reign, the British East India Company was granted important **trading privileges**, such as duty-free trade in Bengal, which later became a cornerstone of British economic power in India.
 
• The **farman** issued by Farrukh Siyar in 1717 allowed the East India Company to trade freely without paying customs duties in Bengal, Gujarat, and Hyderabad.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Decline:**
 
 
• Farrukh Siyar's reign symbolizes the decline of the Mughal Empire, with growing autonomy of provincial governors and increasing interference from external powers like the British and the Marathas.
 
• His inability to maintain centralized control led to the fragmentation of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Key Events During Farrukh Siyar's Reign:**
 
 
• The **execution of Banda Singh Bahadur**, the Sikh leader, in 1716 marked the end of a significant Sikh uprising during his rule.
 
• The Sayyid Brothers' dominance and their practice of replacing emperors showcased the diminished authority of the Mughal throne.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options:**

 
 
• **Ahmad Shah:** He ruled from **1748 to 1754**, long after Farrukh Siyar's reign.
 
• **Shah Alam II:** He ruled from **1759 to 1806**, during the later Mughal period, after the British had already gained significant control in India.
 
• **Alamgir II:** He was the Mughal emperor from **1754 to 1759**, after the assassination of Ahmad Shah Bahadur.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Farrukh Siyar's Reign:**
 
 
• His reign was critical in shaping the Mughal Empire's interactions with European powers, especially the British East India Company.
 
• The decline of the central authority during his rule set the stage for the eventual disintegration of the Mughal Empire.
